guide.name: Figma OAuth Setup and Launch Guide
guide.summary: External customer connections need a public Figma OAuth app and Figma approval. Validate the callback and minimum scopes in a draft first.
guide.timeNote: Planning estimate, not a measured setup duration. Assumes existing OAuth callback and Figma developer account
guide.review: Draft apps can be tested by their creator and admins for that plan. Published private apps serve users in the associated team or organization without Figma review. Public apps need Figma approval before other users can authorize them; every user still grants their own consent. External customers require the public path.
guide.scopeNote: The reviewed Figma instructions map file-content reads to file_content:read. Extra actions need their own endpoint-to-scope check. Scopes do not override the user's access to a file.
prerequisites: A Figma account and a team or organization to own the app.
The integration's callback URLs and a list of intended API actions.
Secure server-side storage for the client secret shown during app creation.

steps.title: Create the draft and save its secret
steps.detail: Create the app at figma.com/developers/apps and associate it with a team or organization. Store the client secret securely before closing creation: it is shown only once. Draft testing is limited to the creator and admins for that plan.

steps.title: Configure callbacks, scopes, and audience
steps.detail: Register the callback URLs used by your integration and select scopes for the intended endpoints. For this file-content-only request, use file_content:read. Choose a public app for external customers; a private app only serves users in its associated team or organization.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code promptly
steps.detail: Exchange the code within 30 seconds at https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/token using a form-encoded POST and HTTP Basic client authentication. Use the same redirect URI. If using the recommended S256 PKCE flow, send the verifier in the token request.

steps.title: Clear the correct publishing gate
steps.detail: Private apps need no Figma review but are limited to the associated team or organization. External customers need an approved public app. Supply its logo, description, testing instructions, and reviewer access where necessary. Approval permits distribution; each user still grants consent. No review turnaround is established here.

steps.title: Handle User Consent
steps.detail: Provide an authentication URL for users to consent to the OAuth app's scopes (s1). Handle the callback and token exchange. Ensure the user's consent is obtained before making API requests on their behalf. Use the provided Client ID and Client Secret to exchange tokens.

steps.title: Monitor and Update App
steps.detail: Monitor the app's usage and update the scopes or configuration as needed (s3). Ensure the app complies with Figma's API terms and guidelines. Re-publish the app if changes are made to the configuration or scopes. Keep the Client ID and Client Secret secure.

blockers.title: Missing Client ID or Client Secret
blockers.detail: Re-register the OAuth app or retrieve the Client ID and Client Secret from the Figma developer dashboard (s1).

blockers.title: The callback must match a registered redirect URL
blockers.detail: The authorization callback must be registered for the app, and the token request must use the same redirect URI. A universal HTTPS-only provider requirement was not verified here.
blockers.resolution: Register the integration's callback and compare the complete URI across app settings, authorization, and token exchange. Choose HTTPS for production as a deployment recommendation; confirm acceptance of any development callback in Figma's app settings instead of inferring a restriction from examples.

blockers.title: Match pilot and launch users to the app audience
blockers.detail: Draft testing is limited to the creator and plan admins; a private app serves its associated team or organization.
blockers.resolution: For the stated external audience, publish a public app, provide reviewer materials, and wait for Figma approval before inviting those users. Then test each user's separate consent.

Configure the exact integration callback and keep any client secret in secure server-side storage.

Confirm production eligibility and complete any provider review required for the selected scopes and audience.
